title: Dallas Fed Texas Service Sector Outlook Survey (Dec 2026 data) — 9:30 a.m. CT / 10:30 ET, the year's last regional survey, sharing its morning with the 7-Year auction's session
source: EST: dallasfed.org's own Texas Service Sector Outlook Survey page (dallasfed.org/research/surveys/tssos), fetched direct 2026-09-09 with a desktop user-agent (HTTP 200) and quoted VERBATIM from its own markup. The table headed `2026 Release Dates` carries the column header `Release (9:30 a.m. CT)` and the row `December | Tuesday, Dec. 29`, alongside the same publishing caveat its manufacturing sibling carries. The same table's `November | Tuesday, Dec. 1` row is the one this calendar's existing dallas-fed-tssos-2026-12-01 entry was filed against — note the series' one-month reporting lag, which is why the December SURVEY publishes on 2026-12-29 and the November one published on 2026-12-01. Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a regional Reserve Bank's own survey schedule, and this lane never self-confirms an event it discovered in-sweep. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of treasury-2y-note-2026-12-28, 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED 2026-09-09 by the treasury-2y-note-2026-12-28 never-assessed initial research, at D+1 of its corridor. WHY IT IS A GAP AND NOT A DUPLICATE: this calendar carries dallas-fed-tssos-2026-12-01 (the November survey) and nothing after it; December is the missing member of the same monthly series, read from the same primary in the same fetch as its manufacturing sibling. WHY IT EARNS A ROW: 2026-12-29 is the 7-Year auction session (treasury-7y-note-2026-12-29, already canonical) and already carries consumer-confidence-2026-12-29 and fhfa-hpi-2026-12-29; adding the two regional surveys this sweep found makes the D+1 crowding visible to the window arithmetic instead of leaving it to be inferred. It also matters to the proposing event specifically: D+1 is the reversal window a soft or strong 12-28 auction would be read against, and the proposing research's honest limit is that this whole corridor is too crowded for a close-to-close attribution.
